predecessors.name: Margraviate of Baden
predecessors.text: the Margraviate of Baden (about 3,500 km2 around 1789, 'united under Charles Frederick' in 1789), the core of the Electorate

predecessors.name: Prince-Bishopric of Constance
predecessors.text: the Bishopric of Constance and the abbeys of Petershausen and Salem, with the imperial cities of Überlingen and Pfullendorf, on and around Lake Constance

predecessors.name: Prince-Bishopric of Speyer
predecessors.text: the right bank of the Speyer bishopric: Bruchsal and Odenheim

predecessors.name: Prince-Bishopric of Strasbourg
predecessors.text: the right bank of the Strasbourg bishopric

successors.name: Grand Duchy of Baden
successors.text: the Electorate, enlarged by Breisgau and other Austrian lands at Pressburg (26 December 1805); Baden 'declared sovereignty' and Charles Frederick became Grand Duke in 1806

ledger.x: 1803: the Imperial Recess makes Baden an electorate under Charles Frederick.
1803: the Speyer lands on the right bank.
1803: the Strasbourg lands on the right bank.
1805/1806: the Electorate becomes the sovereign Grand Duchy.

wars.name: War of the Third Coalition
wars.outcome: French victory; the Peace of Pressburg of 26 December 1805 gave Baden Breisgau and other Austrian lands.

certainty.note: The pages name lands, abbeys and cities, not boundary lines; the Lake Constance and Palatine frontiers are approximate.
